newsitem.title: INDIA: India call inactive, gilt prices continue rising.
newsitem.headline: India call inactive, gilt prices continue rising.

text.p: Indian call money was inactive on Friday while security prices firmed up marginally in brisk trade, dealers said.
"Being the reporting day, there was no action in call money today," a dealer said.

Dealers said there was some uncertainty over interest rates for the next fortnight although some market participants expected call money to remain range bound between 10 percent and 11 percent through the fortnight.
"Call money rates would remain firm as bank balance sheets would be bloated on account of window-dressing for the half yearly closing of accounts on Septmeber 30," a dealer at a state-run bank said.
Dealers said 14-day money was quoted around 10 percent on Friday.

Yields on government securities in the secondary market continued to fall as buying pressure drove prices up, dealers said. The zero-coupon bond maturing in 1999 was traded at a yield of 13.97 percent on Friday against the previous day's 14.06 percent, they said.
The zero-coupon 2000 was traded at 14.03 percent against 14.13 percent. Prices of other securities were stable, they said.
Dealers said three-month commercial paper issued by top-rated companies was quoted 13.50-14.0 percent in the primary market.
In certificates of deposit (CDs), there were a few interbank deals between 13 percent and 13.5 percent for three-month CDs, dealers said.
Rates on intercorporate deposits remained steady in the 17.0-19.0 percent range for top-rated companies but few deals were reported, dealers said.
